html:
SMTO-SKL-0147 — Slack couldn't accept the details of this request

GUID: 448dd240-6773-5118-92c6-6d0f24253dc7
Slug: slack-invalid-arguments
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • Something in the request didn't fit what Slack or SMTO accepts, such as a channel name instead of its ID, a message that's too long, or an unsupported button or image. Slack wasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to look up the channel or person first, then use that exact channel or person, rather than a typed name. Slack actions need the exact channel, person or message, not a name that might match several.
  2. Keep the message under 4,000 characters and use plain text or simple sections. Buttons, images and other extras aren't supported. SMTO only sends simple message layouts to Slack, so extras are refused.
  3. For reactions, give the emoji name as Slack shows it, such as thumbsup, without spaces. Slack rejects emoji names it doesn't recognise.
  4. If you gave a date range, make sure the start comes before the end. A range that ends before it starts can't be read.

What success looks like

  • The Agent completes the Slack read or change without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or your Slack connection. Repeating the same request without changing it will be refused again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Slack operation was rejected by local schema validation (unknown operation or method, wrong ID/timestamp format, out-of-range field, unsupported Block Kit) or by Slack with invalid_arguments, invalid_blocks or invalid_name.

What this means

  • Operation/method lookup or schema validation rejects unsupported names, field shapes, bounds or Block Kit structures, or Slack reports invalid argument/block/name reasons. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Operation/method lookup or schema validation rejects unsupported names, field shapes, bounds or Block Kit structures, or Slack reports invalid argument/block/name reasons.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the concrete local schema or safe provider reason with exact IDs and string timestamps.

How to fix it

  • Check the arguments against slack/models.py: channel IDs match ^[CDG][A-Z0-9]+, user IDs ^[UW]..., file IDs ^F..., timestamps are strings like 1712345678.123456, text is at most 4,000 characters, blocks are at most ten section/divider blocks, reaction names are 1-64 characters of letters, digits, '_', '+' or '-', and oldest is not after latest. Extra fields are rejected.
  • Use exact channel IDs and string timestamps, bounded fields and supported Block Kit sections/dividers; arbitrary payload fields are rejected.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberate supported structured request passes validation.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
